- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent high for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish abruptly (e.g., +0.67 in 1–2 days), model lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8% per sentiment change day.
- When news volume is low (≤1.0) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates; add 0.2–0.7% to forecast to account for suppressed volatility.
- Mean reversion occurs when sentiment is volatile (±0.33 change in 2 consecutive days) and price is above 10-day moving average; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently positive and price is rising, model tends to overfit trend; apply 1–2% downward correction after 3 consecutive bullish sentiment days.
